title: Natural finite-support normal form from a continuous coset section
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent site of profinite sets [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite group $J$, let $\mathcal A_J(A)$ denote internal $A$-modules with $A$-linear condensed $J$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $P$ be a profinite group and $H$ a closed subgroup. For each profinite test set $S$ put $P_S=C(S,P)$ and $H_S=C(S,H)$. The group algebra $A(S)[P_S]$ consists of finite formal sums with multiplication $[p][p']=[pp']$. For $M\in\mathcal A_H(A)$ put $B_M(S)=A(S)[P_S]\otimes_{A(S)[H_S]}M(S)$.

Give $X=\{pH:p\in P\}$ its quotient topology. Assume $X$ is profinite and $q:P\to X$ has a continuous section $s:X\to P$ with $qs=1_X$. Put $X_S=C(S,X)$. For $p\in P_S$ define $x_p=q\circ p$ and $h_p=(s\circ x_p)^{-1}p$, a continuous map $S\to H$. The maps $p\mapsto(x_p,h_p)$ and $(x,h)\mapsto(s\circ x)h$ are inverse bijections $P_S\cong X_S\times H_S$, natural under precomposition of test sets.

Let $D_M(S)=\bigoplus_{x\in X_S}M(S)$ denote the module of finitely supported families, with $e_x(m)$ the family supported at $x$ having coefficient $m$. Restriction along $t:T\to S$ sends $e_x(m)$ to $e_{x\circ t}(t^*m)$; coefficients are added when indices become equal. Give $B_M$ the restriction $[p]\otimes m\mapsto[p\circ t]\otimes t^*m$. Then the formulas
$$\alpha_{M,S}([p]\otimes m)=e_{x_p}(h_p\cdot m),\qquad\beta_{M,S}(e_x(m))=[s\circ x]\otimes m$$
define inverse $A(S)$-linear maps. They commute with restrictions along every map $T\to S$ and with every equivariant coefficient map $u:M\to M'$, where $D_u(e_x(m))=e_x(u(m))$. Thus they give an isomorphism of $A$-module presheaves $B_M\cong D_M$ natural in $M$. There is no normality, finite-index or discreteness hypothesis.

proof.text: For $p:S\to P$, equality $q(s(q(p(z))))=q(p(z))$ says $s(q(p(z)))^{-1}p(z)\in H$ for every $z\in S$. Hence $h_p$ takes values in $H$; it is continuous into the subspace $H$, since inversion, multiplication, $s$, $q$ and $p$ are continuous. For $x:S\to X$ and $h:S\to H$, right multiplication by $h(z)$ fixes the right coset, so $x_{(s\circ x)h}=x$ and $h_{(s\circ x)h}=h$. Conversely $(s\circ x_p)h_p=p$. These prove the inverse bijections, and substitution gives $x_{p\circ t}=x_p\circ t$ and $h_{p\circ t}=h_p\circ t$ for every $t:T\to S$.

proof.text: Fix $S$ and abbreviate $R=A(S)$, $G=P_S$, $K=H_S$, $V=M(S)$. The action definition gives $R$-linear $K$-operators on $V$, hence the group-ring action $(\sum b_k[k])v=\sum b_k(kv)$. Unpack the balanced tensor using symbols $[g]\otimes v$: they generate over $R$, are additive and $R$-linear in $v$, and satisfy $[gk]\otimes v=[g]\otimes kv$. These relations present $R[G]\otimes_{R[K]}V$: a linear symbol map $F(g,v)$ extends to $(\sum a_g[g],v)\mapsto\sum a_gF(g,v)$, and its $R[K]$-balancing is precisely $F(gk,v)=F(g,kv)$, by expansion of finite sums in both group rings. Thus specifying such symbol values defines a unique map out of the tensor; equality can also be checked on these generators.

proof.text: The module $D_M(S)$ is, by definition, the finitely supported families of coefficients in $M(S)$. Every family $v$ is the finite sum $\sum_{x\in\operatorname{supp}(v)}e_x(v_x)$. Consequently $R$-linear maps $f_x:M(S)\to W$ extend uniquely by $v\mapsto\sum_x f_x(v_x)$. More generally, for a ring map $\phi:R\to R'$, a $\phi$-semilinear $f:V\to V'$ and an index map $r:I\to I'$, the finite-sum formula $\sum_i e_i(v_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_{r(i)}(f(v_i))$ is well defined and semilinear. Its coefficient at $j$ is $\sum_{r(i)=j}f(v_i)$ over the finite support; no injectivity of $r$ is required.

proof.text: Put $F(p,m)=e_{x_p}(h_p m)$. This is $R$-linear in $m$. For $k\in H_S$, the right-coset identities give $x_{pk}=x_p$ and $h_{pk}=h_pk$. Therefore $F(pk,m)=e_{x_p}(h_p(km))=F(p,km)$ by the group-action law. The symbol presentation in step 2 defines $\alpha_{M,S}$ with the claimed formula. The finite-sum construction in step 3 defines $\beta_{M,S}$ by the linear maps $m\mapsto[s\circ x]\otimes m$.

proof.text: Since $q s=1_X$, one has $x_{s\circ x}=x$ and $h_{s\circ x}=1$, so $\alpha\beta(e_x(m))=e_x(m)$. In the other order the balanced relation gives $\beta\alpha([p]\otimes m)=[s\circ x_p]\otimes(h_pm)=[(s\circ x_p)h_p]\otimes m=[p]\otimes m$. Finite-sum generation from steps 2 and 3 now proves both inverse identities on all elements, not just generators.

proof.text: For $t:T\to S$, the maps $A(S)\to A(T)$ and $M(S)\to M(T)$ are compatible with scalars and satisfy $t^*(km)=(k\circ t)t^*m$ by the action definition. Hence the proposed restriction on $B_M$ respects additivity, scalar relations and balancing: both $[pk]\otimes m$ and $[p]\otimes km$ restrict to $[p\circ t]\otimes (k\circ t)t^*m$. The restriction on $D_M$ is exactly step 3 with index map $x\mapsto x\circ t$; its formula sums coefficients when this map is not injective. On generators the identity and composition laws reduce to those of restriction on $A,M$ and of precomposition. Thus these formulas define the stated module presheaves.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-formulated sectionwise normal-form input to exact condensed induction; explicit elementary argument below, not an assertion made in the source paragraph.

proof.text: The restriction of $\alpha_{M,S}([p]\otimes m)$ to $T$ equals $e_{x_p\circ t}(t^*(h_pm))=e_{x_{p\circ t}}((h_p\circ t)t^*m)$, which is $\alpha_{M,T}$ applied to the restriction of $[p]\otimes m$. For $\beta$, restriction of $[s\circ x]\otimes m$ is $[s\circ(x\circ t)]\otimes t^*m$. Finally, an equivariant coefficient map satisfies $u_S(h_pm)=h_pu_S(m)$, so $D_u\alpha_M=\alpha_{M'}B_u$ on $[p]\otimes m$, and $B_u\beta_M=\beta_{M'}D_u$ on $e_x(m)$. Finite sums prove these identities even when restricted indices coincide. The inverse maps therefore form the required presheaf isomorphism, natural in $M$.
